package_info.why_malicious: The package is explicitly designed to steal Discord user tokens and browser information by scanning local directories for credential storage, collecting system and user data, and exfiltrating this information to an attacker-controlled Discord webhook. It masquerades as a legitimate module, employs typosquatting, and ensures execution of its malicious payload both at install time and runtime, violating user trust and security.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At install-time, the postinstall script executes the main app.js file, initiating the malicious logic that collects sensitive user data and prepares it for exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Executing arbitrary code during the installation phase is a common malware tactic to guarantee payload execution, even if the package is never imported or used directly.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate npm packages typically use postinstall scripts for build processes or environment setup, not for launching code that accesses user data or initiates network communication.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use postinstall for compiling native modules or checking dependencies, but not for accessing or exfiltrating user data.
key_indicators: postinstall script executes main application logic
no legitimate build or setup task present
triggers data collection and exfiltration at install-time

execution_context.file_location: app.js and classes/Grabber.js, Token.js, User.js, Util.js

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code iterates through browser and Discord data directories, reads LevelDB files to extract Discord tokens and browser credentials, collects system and user information, and retrieves the public IP address, aggregating all data for exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing LevelDB files in browser and Discord directories to extract authentication tokens and user information is a direct indicator of credential theft and privacy violation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not access or parse LevelDB files in browser or Discord directories, nor do they aggregate user tokens, system information, or public IP addresses without explicit user consent.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Forensics or backup utilities may access such data with clear user authorization, but not in a package purporting to be a Discord utility.
key_indicators: Direct access to browser and Discord LevelDB files
Extraction of Discord tokens and user/system information
Use of external IP lookup service (api.ipify.org)
Aggregation of sensitive data for exfiltration

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, after data collection, the code sends the aggregated tokens and user information to an attacker-controlled Discord webhook via an HTTPS POST request, resulting in credential exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Transmitting sensitive user data, including authentication tokens, to an external Discord webhook is a clear sign of information-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not transmit user tokens, browser data, or system information to external servers, especially not via Discord webhooks.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Webhooks are used for legitimate notifications or integrations, but never for exfiltrating user credentials or sensitive data.
key_indicators: Outgoing HTTPS POST to Discord webhook endpoint
Payload contains sensitive user and credential data
No user notification or consent for data transmission

attack_chain.action: Malicious code is executed during package installation via the postinstall script, launching the main app.js file.
attack_chain.leads_to: Initiates the main malicious logic responsible for data collection.

attack_chain.action: The main script scans browser and Discord directories, extracts tokens and user/system information, and collects the public IP address.
attack_chain.leads_to: Aggregates the stolen data and prepares it for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: The collected data is sent to an attacker-controlled Discord webhook via HTTPS POST.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker receives stolen credentials and user information.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of arbitrary code during npm install via postinstall script that launches main application logic
Access to LevelDB files in browser and Discord data directories for credential extraction
Collection and aggregation of Discord tokens, browser credentials, system/user information, and public IP address
Network requests to Discord webhooks containing sensitive user data
file_indicators: Presence of a postinstall script in package.json that executes 'node .' or similar main entrypoint
References in code to browser and Discord data directories (e.g., '%LocalAppData%/Google/Chrome/User Data/Default', '%AppData%/discord')
Files named Grabber.js, Token.js, Webhook.js, or similar credential-grabbing modules
network_indicators: Outgoing HTTPS POST requests to discord.com/api/webhooks/*
Requests to https://api.ipify.org/?format=json for public IP retrieval
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor npm packages for postinstall scripts that execute main application code. Flag any code that accesses LevelDB files in browser or Discord directories. Detect network requests to Discord webhooks, especially those containing tokens or user/system data. Look for package files or code referencing credential grabbing or browser data extraction. Correlate the presence of these behaviors to identify malicious packages.
